issues.legal_issue: A landlord’s pending rent-control eviction claim founded on the landlord’s own personal residential requirement does not survive to legal representatives when the landlord dies before an eviction decree and their distinct requirements would have to replace the original claim.
material_facts: The landlord sought eviction on the ground that the premises were bona fide required for the landlord’s residence with dependent family members and that no other reasonably suitable residential accommodation was available.

The initial eviction application was dismissed on a preliminary issue concerning the notices to quit, and the landlord died while an appeal was pending, before a decision on the merits or an eviction decree.
The landlord’s legal representatives sought to continue the proceeding; determining their requirements and accommodation would involve issues distinct from those pleaded by the landlord.
issues.conclusion: The landlord’s right to sue did not survive to the legal representatives, and they could not continue the pending eviction proceeding on the basis of their own distinct requirements.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order 22 Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure, abatement depends on whether the right to sue survives. The right to sue means the right to seek the same relief that the deceased plaintiff asserted at death, as stated in Saraj Chandra v. Nani Mihan. The nature of the pleaded claim determines survival. Here, the landlord’s claim under section 14(1)(e) of the Delhi Rent Control Act rested on the landlord’s own bona fide requirement, and replacing it with the legal representatives’ distinct requirements would fundamentally alter the pleadings beyond the permissible scope of Order 6 Rule 17 of the Code. The Court treated section 306 of the Indian Succession Act only as an indirect analogy. It distinguished Motilal Pannalal v. Kailash Narain, Amar Nath Bihari v. Jai Dayal Puri, Smt. Dhan Devi v. Bakshi Ram, Vas Dev v. Sohan Singh, Dr. Muhammad Ibrahim v. Rahiman Khan, and Rameshwar Dayal v. Smt. Mohania because those decisions involved different procedural circumstances or principles.

rule.if: rent_control_eviction_proceeding and landlord_died_before_eviction_decree and claim_based_on_landlords_personal_requirement and heirs_require_distinct_factual_inquiry

predicates.rent_control_eviction_proceeding: The proceeding was brought by a landlord to obtain eviction under rent-control law.
predicates.landlord_died_before_eviction_decree: The landlord died while the eviction proceeding was pending and before an eviction decree had been obtained.
predicates.claim_based_on_landlords_personal_requir: The landlord pleaded that the premises were bona fide required for the landlord’s own residence with dependent family members.
predicates.heirs_require_distinct_factual_inquiry: Continuing the proceeding for the legal representatives would require deciding their distinct requirements and accommodation rather than the landlord’s pleaded requirement.

issues.definition: When a landlord dies before an eviction decree in a rent-control proceeding based on the landlord’s personal requirement, and the heirs’ claims require a distinct factual inquiry, the original right to sue does not survive.
